title: D.C. United fires head coach Rene Weiler, expected to hire Oscar Pareja: Sources
content:
D.C. United has fired head coach Rene Weiler, sources briefed on the situation tell The Athletic, and is expected to hire Oscar Pareja to replace him.

Weiler joined the club during the 2025 season. D.C. United finished 14th in the Eastern Conference with 33 points, missing the playoffs by 13 points.

Pareja left Orlando City this spring after a successful run with the club dating back to the 2020 season, leading them to the playoffs in each of his six full seasons in charge. Pareja helped change a club that had missed the playoffs in their first five MLS seasons.

Pareja guided Orlando to win their first-ever trophy in the club’s MLS era, the 2022 U.S. Open Cup.

That kind of stability and success is much-needed in D.C. The club has missed the playoffs in each of the last seven seasons and Pareja will be looking for their fifth full-time head coach since 2021.

D.C.’s squad is headlined by forwards Tai Baribo and Louis Munteanu.

Weiler has bounced around in his managerial career, not lasting two full seasons in a job since FC Aarau from 2011-2014.

The environment behind the scenes at D.C. soured between Weiler and management, sources briefed on the situation told The Athletic. That combined with the poor results makes it unsurprising the club decided to move on.

D.C. spent significant roster assets this year, including two designated player slots on Baribo and Munteanu. The club also added the likes of Sean Johnson, Sean Nealis, Nathan Ordaz and others.

The club ended the season with six straight losses and only one win in their last 11 games.

Before his time with Orlando, Pareja spent five seasons with FC Dallas, winning the Supporters’ Shield and Open Cup in 2017. Pareja is known for youth development, another area of D.C. that needs improvement.

Pareja ended his playing career in the United States with FC Dallas. He won 11 caps for the Colombia national team. He has also been a head coach at the Colorado Rapids and Club Tijuana.
